verdict.rationale: Bitwarden documents an OAS3-compliant Public API with a published swagger.json, a vendor-hosted Swagger UI and a stated backwards-compatibility policy. For vault items, it documents a separate Vault Management API, a local RESTful API served by `bw serve` in the official CLI, which has its own OpenAPI document. Together these let an agent drive both organization administration and vault contents through documented APIs. Missing for 10: vault item access through a hosted public API (the cloud Public API covers only organization members, collections, groups, event logs and policies, while vault access needs the local `bw serve` server), and independent or hands-on corroboration of real API calls (the probe only confirmed the CLI installs, and the root-level openapi.json paths returned 404).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Bitwarden Public API provides organizations a suite of tools for managing members, collections, groups, event logs, and policies.
is compatible with the OpenAPI Specification (OAS3) and publishes a compliant swagger.json definition file
bitwarden.com/help/api/ vendor-hosts Swagger UI over the Public API's embedded OpenAPI 3.0.4 document
we aim to provide backwards compatibility to the API indefinitely through semantic versioning
documented `bw serve` mode exposes the whole vault as a local RESTful API (Vault Management API)
